review_notes:
I read the whole target file and the base-change API in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/BaseChange.lean (baseChangeFDRepUnitIso, baseChangeFDRepTensorIso). I also read `LinearEquiv.toFDRepIso` and `FDRep.isoToEquiv` in FDRep.lean and the sibling GroupAlgebra/BaseChange.lean. I considered several other repetitions and did not report them:
- The `induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn` blocks in baseChangeK0_id, baseChangeK0_comp, and the unit and tensor isos. They differ in their pure-tensor goals, and comp needs a second, nested induction, so a shared lemma would cover only the outer 3-line induction.
- The twin private lemmas coe_map_baseChangeFDRep_f and coe_map_baseChangeFDRep_g, which are thin wrappers.
The reported finding is modest: the shared part is about 3 lines, used in two places. A helper would mainly remove the `FDRep.of_ρ'` rewriting and intertwining-unpacking boilerplate. I did not check how the helper would elaborate with the `FDRep.of` coercions, so the proposed signature may need small adjustments.

findings.problem: The step that turns a `Representation.Equiv` between the actions of two `FDRep.of` objects into an isomorphism in `FDRep` is done by hand. It rewrites `FDRep.of_ρ'` twice and then feeds `IntertwiningMap.isIntertwining` of `e.toIntertwiningMap` to `toFDRepIso`. The same reasoning appears in `groupAlgebraBaseChangeK0_comp_indK0` in GrothendieckGroup/GroupAlgebra/BaseChange.lean. There the equivalence is `e`, the same `e.toLinearEquiv.toFDRepIso fun g x => ?_` is used, and the proof closes with `simpa only [FDRep.of_ρ', ...Equiv.toLinearEquiv_apply] using ...isIntertwining _ _ e.toIntertwiningMap g x`. `FDRep.isoToEquiv` already provides the converse direction (iso to Equiv), but the Equiv-to-iso direction exists only as the pointwise constructor `LinearEquiv.toFDRepIso`. Every caller must therefore redo the unfolding of `FDRep.of` and the intertwining unpacking.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma-level constructor next to `LinearEquiv.toFDRepIso` and `FDRep.isoToEquiv` in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/FDRep.lean. Its signature is `noncomputable def Representation.Equiv.toFDRepIso {ρ : Representation R G V} {σ : Representation R G W} [Module.Finite R V] [Module.Finite R W] (e : ρ.Equiv σ) : FDRep.of ρ ≅ FDRep.of σ`. Prove it as `e.toLinearEquiv.toFDRepIso fun g x => by rw [FDRep.of_ρ', FDRep.of_ρ']; exact Representation.IntertwiningMap.isIntertwining _ _ e.toIntertwiningMap g x`. Optionally add a simp lemma for its underlying linear equivalence. Then `baseChangeK0_of_ofMulAction` becomes `rw [baseChangeK0_of, FDRep.of_ρ']; exact ExactK0.of_congr (baseChangeOfMulActionEquiv k k' G X).toFDRepIso`. The group-algebra proof becomes `refine ExactK0.of_congr e.toFDRepIso` after its `let e`. Take care that the source object in the target proof is `FDRep.of (baseChange k' (FDRep.of ...).ρ)`, so keep the existing `rw [baseChangeK0_of, FDRep.of_ρ']` (or an equivalent `show`) before applying the constructor.
findings.benefit: The `FDRep.of_ρ'` unfolding and the intertwining unpacking are written once, next to the existing constructor and its converse. This gives a symmetric `FDRep.isoToEquiv` / `Equiv.toFDRepIso` API. Each call site shrinks to one line, which makes it clearer that the proof is just 'the equivalence of representations gives an isomorphism of classes'. Any future Equiv-based class comparison (induction, restriction, base change) can reuse the helper.
